why: Rule 1: both prongs cool at 16002 and Bragg at their far ends (163cm mu to 16001, 37cm p to 16000), 98 deg opening, and the zoom shows a dQ/dx jump across the junction so it is two particles not a kink.

Only a 74cm flat-MIP track with no Bragg at either end; the rule-1 'rises away from 24000' is an edge artifact at the y=-198 wall, so I took the interior, lower-z end 24001 which also has a small e blip 5cm off. Close to a guess.

Two Bragg ends in one chain point away from 9003: the 93cm muon rises to 105k at 9000 and the 4.4cm stub rises monotonically to 330k at 9002 (stopping proton); a single particle cannot Bragg at both ends. Tier dropped because the two prongs are 168 deg apart (collinear trap).

Clusters 9 and 61 are one ~32cm stopping proton (dQ/dx 52k at 9000 to 125k at 9001 to 240k at 61053, matching the proton range-energy curve), so its cool end 9000 is the start; shower fragments 58/46030/45028 sit within 6cm of it.

The single 2.2cm 139k proton stub is the only real deposit and localises the interaction to within about 2cm, so I named it rather than abstaining; with no p4 panel there is no profile to orient the stub, and the choice between its two ends 9000/9001 is a coin flip broken only by rule 2.

Rule 6/7 on a compact 65cm shower: 4003 is the only real junction (deg 4, prongs of 21.9 and 15.5cm plus a 3/4.6cm stub), sits at the upstream low-x corner, and the whole spray including the six satellite blips opens away from it. Rule 1 fails there but three particles cannot all stop at one point, so I read it as a dense EM start.

Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away at 140 deg, and the zoom shows a sharp dQ/dx step across 7004 (100k proton side, 50k MIP side); the 45cm muon Braggs to 135k at 7005 where a 13cm decay prong hangs, so rule 3 makes 7005 the far end.

Single 242cm muon with a clean monotone Bragg at 5000 (170k falling over the first 10cm), so rule 1 and rule 2 both put the start at 5001, which is interior, beam-forward and lowest z; tier held below certain because the zoom shows a bare track end with nothing attached, so the call rests on one prong only.

Rule 1 textbook: a 5.6cm dark-red proton stub (210-310k) and a 273cm MIP muon that Braggs to 190k at the far end 8000 both leave 8001 cool, opening 71 deg, and 8001 is the lowest-z point of the cluster.

Rule 1 on a deg-3 hadronic vertex: a 21.7cm proton Bragging to 180k at 11000, a 7.5cm prong rising to 163k at 11001 and a 2.7cm 186k stub all leave 11002, which is the local dQ/dx minimum in the zoom.

The upstream group (z 80-145) holds far more charge than the downstream EM fragments, and within it rule 1 is clean at 19002: the 39.5cm proton Braggs to 235k at 19000 and cools to its start at 19002. The rival hot stub cluster 65 is 42cm away and the proton does not point back at it.

Rule 1 with 2 of 2 rising away at a clear 126 deg V: the 77cm muon Braggs to 210k at 16000 and the 21.6cm pion Braggs to 180k at 16003, where a 4.9cm proton starts and Braggs to 265k, so 16003 is a pion secondary and 16002 is the vertex.

Clusters 13 and 39 are one straight 330cm flat-MIP track (the join is 2cm and 173 deg, a reconstruction split), with no Bragg anywhere; one end lies on the y=+200 wall, so I took the interior, lowest-z end 39020, which has three or four sub-cm blips within 25cm as the hadronic recoil.

Ignoring the 317cm crossing track, the compact complex at (-45,-105,420) gives 40034 as its deg-3 junction with all three prongs non-decreasing away and a hot 6.8cm 110k stub attached, but 17002 and 40031 are nearly as good and the pieces are separated by centimetre-scale gaps.

Rule 1 textbook deg-3 vertex: a 13.4cm proton rising monotonically to 270k at 11001, a 49.9cm proton rising to 145k at 11003 and a 78.7cm flat-MIP muon all leave 11002 cool, and 11002 is the lowest-z point of the cluster.
